To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the lymphocyte mitogenic responses to acute exercise are blunted in the old compared with the young, and the magnitude of this blunting is associated with the magnitude of the exercise-induced increase in circulating lymphocytes.

1) the lymphocyte mitogenic responses to acute exercise are reduced in older adults, and this is associated with a greater exercise-induced leukocytosis; and 2) the exercise-induced leukocystosis is not associated with an increased risk of acute coronary syndromes.
the lymphocytes of older adults are more sensitive to exercise-induced mitogenic stimulation than the lymphocytes of young adults.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of acute exercise on leukocyte count and mitogenic response.
the effects of acute maximal exercise upon leukocytosis, and lymphocyte mitogenesis in the young (20-29 yr) and old (65-75 yr) subjects.
the study of differential leukocytosis (DL) in response to acute maximal physical exercise in the young (20-35 years) and the old (60-70 years).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
exercise training is an effective intervention for improving the quality of life in older adults, but the magnitude of the effects is small and the evidence is of low quality.
exercise is beneficial for the immune system, and that exercise-induced immune responses are dependent on exercise intensity, duration and frequency.
acute exercise is not a potent immunostimulatory stimulus in the young or elderly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that acute maximal exercise results in a differential leukocytosis with an early neutrophilia, a late lymphocytosis and a late monocytosis.
the young and old have different leukocyte responses and lymphocyte mitogenesis following maximal exercise.
the lymphocytes of the old respond to acute exercise with an increased proliferative response to mitogenic stimulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lymphocyte proliferative response to maximal exercise is attenuated in older adults compared to young adults.
the immune system in the elderly is more responsive to exercise, but that it is also less able to respond.
exercise is a powerful tool that can be used to help prevent or treat many diseases, including cancer.
